concept: Small samples swing more. With 15 births a day, more than 60% boys happens on about 15% of days; with 45 a day, only about 7%. Extremes, high and low, come from the small groups.

misconceptions.label: Sample size doesn't matter
misconceptions.why_tempting: Both hospitals have the same 50% chance per baby, so they feel like they should behave the same.
misconceptions.refutation: One extra boy moves a 15-baby day by about 7 points but a 45-baby day by about 2. Small samples hit extreme percentages far more often.
misconceptions.source_note: Tversky & Kahneman hospital problem: 56% chose 'about the same', 22% each chose larger or smaller

misconceptions.label: An extreme small group must have a cause
misconceptions.why_tempting: A story (clean rural air, a good principal) explains an extreme rate better than 'it's a small group'.
misconceptions.refutation: Small groups produce extreme rates in both directions just by chance. If the same kind of place is at both the top and the bottom, size is the explanation.
misconceptions.source_note: Wainer & Zwerling: kidney cancer rates are lowest AND highest in mostly rural, sparsely populated counties

items.prompt: A town has two hospitals. About 45 babies are born each day at the big one and about 15 at the small one. About half of all babies are boys. Over a year, which hospital records more days where more than 60% of the babies born were boys?

truth.x_label: boys out of 15 births in a day

items.prompt: US counties with the lowest kidney cancer rates are mostly rural and sparsely populated. Counties with the HIGHEST rates are... ?

options.text: Mostly big cities: pollution and stress
Also mostly rural and sparsely populated

truth.x_label: cases in a county of 20 people at a 10% rate (toy model)
